edge_explainer: IonQ reported an $805 million profit last quarter on $64.7 million of revenue. It was not a profit: a $1.058 billion warrant fair-value gain, booked because the stock fell, sat on top of a $271.5 million operating loss and $151 million of cash burn in the same three months. The prior-year mirror image confirms it — a $1.055 billion loss in the quarter the stock rose. The finding that matters is not that IonQ hid this, because it did not; it is that our own screen ranked the name at 50.8 partly on vendor fields reading a 99x trailing P/E and a positive 175% net margin. Any screen touching a SPAC-legacy issuer must adjust net income by the warrant line before ranking. On the business itself there is nothing to underwrite: seventy-one times sales, a six-hundred-million-dollar annual burn that is accelerating, a share count up 26% in nine months, 43% of book value in goodwill from stock-funded acquisitions, and a cash floor 87% below the current price. Nor is it shortable — beta 3.3, a strong-buy consensus with a 76% upside target, and ten ten-percent days this year is squeeze fuel, not a borrow.
